newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - March 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - March 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

After accepting a prime position with the player's association, dismissed former Australian Cricket Board chief executive Graham Halbish will enter into negotiations with his former employer. Halbish has denied he is a gamekeeper turned poacher. Page 18.

When the Australian national gymnastics championships begin today at the New South Wales State Sports Centre, the nation's elite female gymnasts will face the challenge of revised international judging rules. The top score of 10 will be much harder to acheve with starting scores now lower. Page 17.

After the Australian women's hockey team's uninspiring 4-3 defeat of Germany in yesterday's fourth test in Sydney yesterday, Olympic hockey coach Ric Charlesworth has threatened to dismiss some of his gold medallists saying he is disappointed with their fitness and commitment. Page 17.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Football League has withdrawn a requirement for the Sydney Swans team to pay back almost $A2 million in licence fees. The AFL has agreed to a Swans request that the club not be force to pay back the amount by the original deadline of Decembr 31, 2004. Page 52.

Under a strict new policy issued by the Australian Human Rights and Equal Opportunities Commission, Australian Rugby League clubs will have to pay fines of $A20,000 if players are found guilty of racial abuse. Page 52.

Australian NSW cricket coach Geoff Lawson has denied the NSW Cricket Association's move to cull his club from the Sydney grade competition would have any influence on his bid to be reappointed, but claimed there was a personal campaign against him. Page 5.
THE AGE

At the Australian cycling championships in Melbourne yesterday, Australian cyclist Lucy Tyler-Sharman crashed through rival Kathy Watt's national record in the 3000 metres individual pursuit and afterwards launched into a verbal assault on her fellow cyclst - calling for Watt to be dropped from the national team. Page B8.
Club captain of Australian Football League team Port Adelaide, Gavin Wanganeen, was suspended for one match last night causing the team's eagerly awaited debut to take place without him. Page B8.

Australian basketballer for the American Chicago Bulls, Luc Longley, had mixed fortunes in the team's match against the Seattle Supersonics yesterday - hitting two key lay-ups and then fouling Seattle's Gary Payton to send the match into overtime. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian drag racer Rachelle Splatt - who is also the nation's fastest woman - will face two races at Calder Park this weekend and wants to win the Top Fuel title at the Nationals meeting. Splatt wants to be the first to break the 300mph (480kmh) drag acing record in this country. Page 78.

Australian horse racing favourite General Nediym was declared yesterday "a risk of Double Trigger proportions" by prominent Sydney bookmaker Geoff Landrey in Saturday's $A2 million Golden Slipper Stakes. Page 80.

Australian Football League players Geelong captain Barry Stoneham and Carlton full-back Stephen Silvagni both seem sure to miss the Ansett Cup Grand Final at the MCG tomorrow night due to respective thigh and hamstring injuries. Page 88.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Some of Australia's top athletes have been warned to consult their doctor after an outbreak of meningitis, believed to have spread during drinking games at a party at the New Zealand national athletic championships on March 9, caused the death of one athlete and the treatment of more than 150 others. Page 78.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor will have his future as a one-day batsman evaluated this week, with the player one failure away from the longest dry spell in Australian Test cricket history. Page 79.

Australian Canberra Raiders rugby league player Quentin Pongia was suspended last night by the Super League judiciary for four matches after the club failed to have the prop's poor record ruled inadmissible. Page 80.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
